sections.markdown:
## C2 — Vehicle emergencies, collision response and crash reporting

FACT_ID: sec18-R01 | anchor: A04
The handbook distinguishes ABS steering while braking from the non-ABS procedure of braking, releasing the brake and then steering. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec18-R02 | anchor: A04
For the described quick turn without ABS, avoid locking the front wheels or turning so sharply that the vehicle continues plowing ahead. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec18-R03 | anchor: A04
If a vehicle threatens to strike from behind or the side and clear space exists ahead, accelerating may help escape; slow again after the danger passes. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec18-R04 | anchor: A04
Wet, snowy or icy surfaces and high speed can increase skid risk during sudden turns or stops. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec18-R05 | anchor: A04
A skid occurs when tires lose their grip on the road. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec18-R06 | anchor: A04
Use both lap and shoulder belts to reduce injury risk when a collision cannot be avoided. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec18-R07 | anchor: A05
Lap and shoulder belts help keep the driver behind the wheel and provide protection if another impact follows the first. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0140]

FACT_ID: sec18-R08 | anchor: A05
If not involved in a crash and emergency help has arrived, do not stop just to watch or block rescue vehicles. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0140]

FACT_ID: sec18-R09 | anchor: A05
When passing a crash, remain attentive to driving and to people near or in the roadway. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0140]

FACT_ID: sec18-R10 | anchor: A05
A driver involved in a crash must stop. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0140]

FACT_ID: sec18-R11 | anchor: A05
After striking a parked vehicle, try to find its owner. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0140]

FACT_ID: sec18-R12 | anchor: A05
If a crash involves injury or death, notify police and remain until they obtain the necessary information. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0140]

FACT_ID: sec18-R13 | anchor: A05
The handbook suggests carrying an emergency kit with warning devices, first-aid supplies and basic tools. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0140]

FACT_ID: sec18-R14 | anchor: A05
After reasonably establishing that no one is injured or dead, a driver whose damaged vehicle blocks traffic must make reasonable efforts to move it or have it moved. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0140]

FACT_ID: sec18-R15 | anchor: A05
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes at a crash scene. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0140]

FACT_ID: sec18-R16 | anchor: A05
Do not smoke near wrecked vehicles because spilled fuel creates fire risk. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0140]

FACT_ID: sec18-R17 | anchor: A05
Stay away from downed power lines or wires lying in the roadway. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0140]

FACT_ID: sec18-R18 | anchor: A05
Warn approaching traffic so the crash does not cause another collision. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0140]

FACT_ID: sec18-R19 | anchor: A06
If someone is injured, ensure police and emergency medical or rescue help have been called, and tell police if fire is present. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0141]

FACT_ID: sec18-R20 | anchor: A06
A driver in a crash causing apparent property damage must stop immediately at the scene. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0141]

FACT_ID: sec18-R21 | anchor: A06
For a crash involving property damage, injury or death, exchange names, addresses, vehicle registration and driver-license numbers, insurer names and policy numbers. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0141]

FACT_ID: sec18-R22 | anchor: A06
Collect names and addresses of people involved in the crash and witnesses, including injured people. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0141]

FACT_ID: sec18-R23 | anchor: A06
If a parked vehicle’s owner cannot be found, leave a visible note with contact details and the crash date and time. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0141]

FACT_ID: sec18-R24 | anchor: A06
Immediately report an injury or fatal crash to the police agency responsible for the location. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0141]

FACT_ID: sec18-R25 | anchor: A06
For a crash on a public highway, apparent property damage of $500 or more triggers immediate reporting to the police agency responsible for that location. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0141]

FACT_ID: sec18-R26 | anchor: A06
The handbook requires immediate police reporting when a crash appears to involve a driver whose physical ability is impaired by alcohol or drugs and apparent property damage reaches $1,000 or more. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0141]

FACT_ID: sec18-R27 | anchor: A07
Roadway problems needing immediate attention, such as damaged signs, debris, signal failures or unsafe work-zone setup, should be reported directly to the DelDOT Transportation Management Center. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0142]
